Azerbaijan Lifts Visas for Citizens of BiH: Top Destinations Worth Visiting

Published: August 3, 2026
Share
SHARE
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:16
Instaread

After Azerbaijan introduced the temporary visa-free regime for citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a new opportunity opens for travel lovers to explore one of the most interesting countries.

From August 1, 2026 to August 1, 2027, citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina who hold regular passports can travel to Azerbaijan without a visa for tourist visits.

This country offers a combination of rich history, oriental culture, impressive nature, and modern architecture. Azerbaijan is a destination where ancient cities and traditions meet futuristic buildings, luxury promenades, and contemporary lifestyle.

The capital city Baku, located on the coast of the Caspian Sea, attracts special attention from tourists. The city represents a unique combination of old and new – while within the walls of the historic core, narrow stone streets and centuries-old buildings are hidden, and a modern part of the city is famous for futuristic edifices, broad boulevards, and impressive sea views.

What to Visit in Baku?

Maiden Tower

One of the most famous buildings in Baku is the Maiden Tower, located at the heart of the Old Town. This 12th-century construction is shrouded in numerous legends, and its original purpose still sparks differing interpretations today.

Some believe it once served as an astronomical facility, while others theorize it was connected to the Zoroastrian tradition. Today it is one of Azerbaijan’s national symbols and a must-visit location for tourists.

Palace of the Shirvanshahs

The Palace of the Shirvanshahs is located in the Old Town, one of Azerbaijan’s most important historical complexes.  Constructed in the 15th century, this palace was once the headquarters of the Shirvanshahs Dynasty and today stands as a valuable example of the country’s architecture and cultural heritage. The complex comprises various rooms, a mausoleum, and a mosque, offering visitors insight into the lives and traditions of former rulers.

Old City Icherisheher

The oldest part of Baku, known as Icherisheher, is one of the places tourists visit the most. Old walls surround it, and its narrow stone streets lead through the city’s past, which was once an important stop on the Silk Road.

While walking in this part of the city, many traditional shops, crafting shops, souvenirs, carpets, and handicrafts characteristic of different parts of Azerbaijan can be found. Visitors can also enjoy local restaurants and cafes, and try a popular pomegranate juice, one of the country’s most recognizable tastes.

Carpet Museum

Azerbaijani culture is known for traditional carpets, and the best insight into this art is offered by the Carpet Museum in Baku. The museum’s structure is an attraction because its appearance resembles a rolled carpet. In the museum, there is a rich collection of traditional and contemporary carpets, which include valuable historical specimens.

Flame Towers

Among the most recognizable symbols of contemporary Baku are the Flame Towers. Three tall structures dominate the city’s panorama, and they are especially attractive at night when their LED lights create flame effects on the facades.

Their appearance is connected to Azerbaijan’s history and its connection with fire, which has a special place in the country’s culture. In addition, fortresses represent a contemporary development of the city, which became one of the most modern regions’ centers last year. 

Miniature Book Museum

For book lovers, the Miniature Book Museum can be an interesting stop. The collection includes several thousand small editions from different parts of the world, and among them is also one of the smallest editions of the Qur’an.

Bibi-Heybat Mosque

The Bibi-Heybat Mosque is located on the coast near Baku, and it is one of the most important religious sites in Azerbaijan. Although the current building was restored, the location has a long history and significance for the local population.

In addition to landmarks, a special part of experiencing Azerbaijan is its cuisine.  It was influenced by Turkish, Persian, and Central Asian traditions. During the stay, it is worth trying traditional dishes such as various kinds of kebabs, fresh salads, homemade bread, and a must-try tea that takes a special place in this country’s culture.

The introduction of a visa-free regime for citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina represents an excellent opportunity for all those who want to discover a new destination, a different culture and country where history and modern architecture meet at every step, Klix.ba writes.
